source_text: Prope est verbum in ore tuo et in corde tuo — hoc est verbum fidei quod praedicamus. Quia si confitearis in ore tuo Dominum Iesum et in corde tuo credideris quod Deus illum suscitavit a mortuis, salvus eris.
thought_title: The word of faith near you
orientation: Origen opens his commentary by quoting Paul's words from Romans 10 about the nearness of the word of faith and the confession that saves.
pass_a_gloss: Near is the word in your mouth and in your heart — this is the word of faith which we preach. Because if you confess in your mouth the Lord Jesus and in your heart you have believed that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved.

choices.why: Matches the glossary term fides as faith and keeps the phrase as a fixed expression from Paul's preaching.
Renders the title Dominus with its full force as Lord, matching the cast name for Jesus Christ.
Keeps the literal force of suscitavit as raised and a mortuis as from the dead, preserving the resurrection language.
rejected: brought him back from the dead

choices.why: Renders the future passive force of salvus eris literally, matching the promise of salvation.

pass_b_english: "The word is near you, in your mouth and in your heart"—that is, the word of faith that we preach. "Because if you confess with your mouth the Lord Jesus and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved" (Romans 10:8-9).
